recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Reopening top-level Observation.value[x] to all datatypes would contradict later applied OO clarification; any desire for non-Quantity top-level vital-sign values should be handled by a new tracker that explicitly supersedes the R6 vital-signs cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-13796 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 OO request to stop the Vital Signs Base profile from constraining Observation.value[x] and Observation.component.value[x] to Quantity and from forcing supporting related observations back to a Vital Signs profile; the example was blood pressure cuff size as a CodeableConcept.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly named FHIR-13796. The 2017 Zulip thread shows the issue was filed from the cuff-size/supporting-observation discussion and records OO approval to relax constraints for supporting observations. Source history shows the old cuff-size/CodeableConcept wording entering the vital-signs profile family in 2018 vitals slicing work, with FHIR-14037 moving the old related/member restriction out of the base profile.
additional_context: Later applied R6 decisions refine the old request. FHIR-31382 removed the confusing implication that cuff size belongs in BP Observation.value[x] and replaced the base value definition with 'The quantity for the vital sign being observed.' FHIR-27800, FHIR-43353, FHIR-47136, and FHIR-48427 moved unit bindings and Must Support requirements so supporting data can be carried as components or related observations without all components being Quantity.
reconciliation: No source change was made. On the current combined branch, Observation.value[x] remains Quantity as later clarified, Observation.component.value[x] has no datatype restriction or unit binding on the unsliced element, the Quantity unit binding is limited to the valueQuantity slice, and Observation.hasMember targets generic Observation.

related_jiras.note: Moved the old related/member constraint out of the base Vital Signs profile, addressing the same supporting-observation association problem.
Clarified that cuff size should not be read as BP Observation.value[x] and that the base value is the quantity for the vital sign.
Ensured component unit bindings apply only to the Quantity/valueQuantity slice rather than all component value datatypes.
Relaxed Vital Signs component quantity unit binding and recognized that coded components such as Korotkoff sounds must not be blocked.
Aligned base result narrative with value, component, hasMember, or dataAbsentReason alternatives.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive OO issue saying the Vital Signs profile should not constrain supporting values to Quantity, with cuff size CodeableConcept as the example.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the seed request and final workflow state.

evidence_items.summary: The 2017 discussion that led to GF#13796 describes cuff size as a supporting observation and records OO approval to relax constraints for supporting observations.
evidence_items.learned: The original interoperability problem was inability to carry supporting data such as cuff size, not a later requirement that every vital-sign Observation.value[x] accept all datatypes.

evidence_items.summary: Observation.value[x] is Quantity, while Observation.component.value[x] is unsliced/generic and only the valueQuantity slice carries the UCUM binding.
evidence_items.learned: Current source permits non-Quantity supporting component values while retaining later quantity semantics for the primary vital-sign value.

evidence_items.summary: Observation.hasMember targets http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Observation rather than only the Vital Signs profile.
evidence_items.learned: The old related/supporting-observation association constraint no longer blocks non-vital-sign supporting observations.

evidence_items.summary: Applied R6 clarification replaced the old cuff-size wording on Observation.value[x] with 'The quantity for the vital sign being observed.' and made component.value[x] generic.
evidence_items.learned: Later WG intent supports treating cuff size as component/supporting data rather than reopening top-level Observation.value[x] for this old issue.

evidence_items.summary: Later Applied component-binding issues ensured Vital Signs component unit bindings apply only to Quantity/valueQuantity, not to coded supporting components.
evidence_items.learned: The component datatype/binding side of the seed concern is already correct in current source and represented by existing combined-branch reconciliations.

evidence_items.summary: Observation is an active resource and the active Observation Vital Signs implementation guide includes StructureDefinition/vitalsigns.
evidence_items.learned: The inspected source is current FHIR-core build-scope source.
